notes.40번|vocab|2: 의식에 떠오르기 전후의 구분에 근거해 consciously→nonconsciously. 다른 어휘와 해설도 타당.
notes.41~42번|vocab: invalidates→legitimizes는 맞지만 해설이 인용문의 빈칸을 반복하다 끝나 실제 교정어와 정당화/확산의 관계를 설명하지 않는다.
notes.41~42번|vocab|2: 기회의 평등·누구나 공적 인물이 됨과 restricted가 모순된다. democratized 교정과 원문 근거 충분.

20번|vocab.blanked: Learning games need to be what we call 'fun enough.' Many new learning-game developers try to design an ①entertaining game. Unfortunately, that often makes learning ②harder rather than easier. Remember, you are not creating the next great commercial game to entertain your learners; you are creating a learning game in which success will be measured by the achievement of learning outcomes. ③Resist the temptation to create a ton of rules, pile on different game elements, and incorporate multiple dynamics to keep player interest high. Yes, the game should be engaging with a mild level of fun, but learning should be the goal. Focus on engagement rather than entertainment. The goals of the game play should be ④interactivity and engagement. Research shows that what makes games instructional is the level of interactivity and engagement the learners have with the content. Given those parameters, making sure the learners are engaged and active is far more important than making sure they are ⑤distracted.
20번|vocab.explanation: ⑤가 정답입니다. 지문은 학습 게임의 목표가 단순한 오락이 아닌 학습 결과의 달성에 있음을 강조합니다. 특히 "Focus on engagement rather than entertainment"라고 명시하며, 학습자가 콘텐츠와 적극적으로 상호작용하며 몰입하는 것이 중요하다고 말합니다. 따라서 문맥상 학습자가 '산만해지거나(distracted)' 있는 것이 아니라 '재미있고(enjoyable/entertained)' 상태여야 한다는 논리가 성립합니다. 'distracted'은 주의가 흩어졌다는 부정적 의미로, 학습 게임의 긍정적 목표와 배치되므로 'entertained'로 수정해야 합니다.

21번|vocab.blanked: We are ①wonderfully made, yet we don't allow ourselves to participate in the wonder for which we were created. Instead of moving anywhere and everywhere, most of us spend our time moving nowhere. We occupy the same square footage of a chair for hours and hours every day. Many kids today are being held ②free by 'smart' devices like phones and tablets. They are not going outside to play, they are not learning how to ③socialize and read physical cues from others. As a result they are not learning or building their movement repertoire, the very thing that will help them learn, communicate, create, and become emotionally mature. They are not even learning how to run, how to skip, or how to climb. Instead, they are learning how to live with ④anxiety, depression, and even diseases they were never meant to have. The point is we are getting further and further away from our design. We were made to move ─ and through movement, we are meant to live ⑤extraordinary lives. Movement is life to us.
21번|vocab.explanation: ②가 정답입니다. 지문에서 'smart' devices에 의해 아이들이 밖으로 나가 놀지 않고, 신체적 단서를 읽는 법을 배우지 못하며, 운동 능력을 키우지 못한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 아이들이 기기에 의해 갇혀 있거나 구속된 상태를 의미하므로, 문맥상 'free(자유로운)'가 아닌 'captive(갇힌, 포로가 된)'가 적절합니다. 따라서 ② free를 captive로 고쳐야 합니다.

22번|vocab.blanked: Perhaps you have heard of the Law of Attraction, which ①states that 'like attracts like' and that by focusing on positive or negative thoughts, one can bring about positive or negative results. The common ②strength in our understanding of this law is that we believe all we have to do is think about or visualize something to manifest it. It is true that we attract at the level of our own vibration and that our thoughts and words are extremely ③magnetic. But the most powerful attractor is our belief system. You can create beautiful poster boards full of images of what you want and affirm every day that you are available for an incredibly successful, passionate career or a loving relationship; but if you don't truly believe you are enough, worthy, lovable, and deserving, then attracting a great career or relationship into your life may be more ④challenging. Consider what limiting beliefs you have that contradict your desires and ⑤upgrade them to beliefs that are in line with what you want to attract.
22번|vocab.explanation: ②가 정답입니다. 앞문장에서 'like attracts like'과 긍정적 사고로 결과를 가져온다는 법의 정의를 설명한 뒤, 뒷문장에서 'It is true that... magnetic'이라고 하여 이 법이 실제로 작동한다는 점을 인정하고 있습니다. 그러나 'But'로 시작하는 문장에서 '가장 강력한 것은 신념 체계'라고 강조하며, 단순히 시각화만으로는 부족하고 진정한 신념이 필요함을 지적합니다. 이는 우리가 이 법을 이해하는 데 있는 일반적인 '결함(flaw)'을 언급하는 것으로, 'strength(강점)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 따라서 'strength'는 'flaw'로 고쳐져야 합니다.

23번|vocab.blanked: It's important for humans to have many kinds of minds, because ①variation is critical for the survival of a species. One of Charles Darwin's greatest insights was that variation is a prerequisite for natural selection to work. Think about it: If there's a huge change in the environment, like a catastrophic drop in the food supply or a big increase in temperature, a species without much variation might be completely wiped out. A species with great variation will more likely have some survivors after any ②catastrophe ─ the members who are well suited for the new environment. Darwin observed variation in the bodies of animals, and the same principle applies to human minds. If we all had the same kind of mind ─ if there were only one human nature ─ then when disaster struck, we might become ③extinct. Thankfully, our species has many kinds of minds, both within a single culture and across cultures, so we're less likely to be wiped out. This variation ④preserves the ⑤stagnation of our species.
23번|vocab.explanation: ⑤가 정답입니다. 지문은 인간의 다양한 사고방식(variation)이 종의 생존(survival)에 필수적이라고 강조합니다. 특히 마지막 문장은 이러한 다양성이 종을 어떻게 하는지 설명해야 하는데, 'stagnation(정체)'은 앞선 문맥인 'wiped out(멸종)'을 피하고 생존하는 긍정적 결과와 모순됩니다. 따라서 다양성이 종의 '진화 가능성(evolvability)'을 보존한다는 의미로 고쳐야 합니다. 앞문장에서 'disaster struck(재난 발생)'과 'less likely to be wiped out(멸종될 가능성이 적다)'는 맥락이 이어지므로, 다양성이 종의 정체성이 아닌 생존과 진화를 가능하게 한다는 논리가 성립합니다.

24번|vocab.blanked: Letting go of our need for control, being aware, is a lot about gathering the courage to face ①uncertainty. Human beings want to know. When we don't know, when things are uncertain, we often feel ②frightened and become inflexible. So we pretend that things are more ③unpredictable than they really are, even though we actually live with enormous uncertainty all the time. We cling to our plans and ideas about how things should be and turn out ever so desperately. And there's nothing wrong with having plans. I think it's a beautiful thing. But there's a difference between planning and thinking all your plans have to come to ④fruition. American president Eisenhower once said: 'Plans are ⑤worthless, but planning is everything.' Imagine if we all used pencil instead of ink to write in our calendars and planners. Both figuratively and literally. Imagine if we could bear in mind that what we write down, what we think is going to happen, might not be what actually happens. And if we could try our best to be all right with that.
24번|vocab.explanation: ③이 정답입니다. 앞문장인 'things are uncertain'과 뒤문장인 'live with enormous uncertainty'를 통해 문맥이 불확실성을 다루고 있음을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 'more unpredictable than they really are'는 '실제보다 더 예측 불가능하다'는 뜻으로, 문맥상 '실제보다 더 예측 가능하다(predictable)'는 의미로 고쳐져야 합니다. 즉, 'unpredictable'은 'predictable'으로 수정되어야 합니다.

29번|vocab.blanked: To understand how breathing affects athletic performance, we first need to understand how the body makes energy from air and food. There are two options: with oxygen, a process known as ①aerobic respiration, and without it, which is called anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic energy is generated only with glucose (a simple sugar), and it's quicker and ②easier for our bodies to access. It's a kind of backup system and turbo boost when the body doesn't have enough oxygen. But anaerobic energy is ③inefficient and can be ④beneficial, creating too much lactic acid. The sickness, muscle weakness, and sweating you experience after you've pushed it too hard at the gym is the feeling of anaerobic overload. This process explains why the first few minutes of an intense workout are often so ⑤miserable. Our lungs and respiratory system haven't caught up to supply the oxygen our bodies need, and so the body has to use anaerobic respiration. This also explains why, after we're warmed up, exercise feels easier. The body has switched from anaerobic to aerobic respiration.
29번|vocab.explanation: ④가 정답입니다. 지문은 무산소 호흡이 근육 약화와 발한, 피로감 등 부정적인 결과를 초래한다고 설명하며, 이를 'anaerobic overload'라고 부릅니다. 이어지는 문장에서는 이러한 상태가 운동 초기에 'miserable(고통스러운)' 느낌을 준다고 명시하고 있으므로, 전체 문맥은 무산소 호흡의 비효율성과 해로움을 강조합니다. 따라서 'too much lactic acid'를 생성하여 건강에 해로운 영향을 미치는 무산소 에너지를 'beneficial(유익한)'이라고 표현하는 것은 문맥상 모순됩니다. 이는 오히려 'toxic(유독한)' 또는 부정적인 의미를 지닌 낱말로 고쳐져야 합니다.

30번|vocab.blanked: Keep your paragraphs ①short. Writing is visual ─ it catches the eye before it has a chance to catch the brain. Short paragraphs put air around what you write and make it look ②inviting, whereas a long chunk of type can discourage a reader from even starting to read. Newspaper paragraphs should be only two or three sentences long; newspaper type is set in a narrow width, and the inches quickly add up. You may think such frequent paragraphing will ③damage the development of your point. Obviously The New Yorker is obsessed by this fear ─ a reader can go for miles without relief. Don't worry; the gains far ④undermine the hazards. But don't go too far. A succession of tiny paragraphs is as annoying as a paragraph that's too long.
